title: Technology Sector Update for 07/24/2018: MDSO,LKM,BABA,GOOG,GOOGL

Technology stocks still were firmer in late afternoon trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.4% in value, retreating from a more than 1% increase earlier in the session, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was sinking about 1.0%, also reversing a nearly 1% gain earlier today.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Medidata Solutions ( MDSO ) tumbled Tuesday, falling almost 14% in late trade, despite the cloud-based data analytics company reporting improved Q2 financial results over year-ago levels, and also topping analyst estimates. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.43 per share during the April-to-June fiscal period, up from $0.30 per share during the same quarter last year and topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.04 per share. Revenue rose to $155.9 million from $136 million last year, largely in-line with the analyst mean. Looking forward, the company is projecting FY18 revenue in a range of $624 million to $648 million, spanning the $640.2 million Street view.
In other sector news:
+ Alphabet (GOOG,GOOGL) climbed to a record high on Tuesday, rising over 5% to a best-ever $1266 a share, after the technology conglomerate reported Q2 operating income and revenue, prompting several analysts to increase their price targets for the company's stock. Excluding a $5 billion anti-trust fine by the European Union the company plans to appeal, Google earned $11.75 per share, up from $8.90 per share last year and exceeding the Street view expecting $9.54 per share. GAAP earnings fell to $4.54 per share from $5.01 per share during the same quarter last year but still also topped the $3.58 a share Capital IQ consensus. Revenue grew to $32.7 billion from $26 billion last year, also surpassing the $32.1 billion Street view.
Following the better-than-expected results, Canaccord raised its price target for Google shares by $20 to $1,170 apiece based on 24 times its projected FY19 earnings of $48.75 per share. Also, Oppenheimer reiterated its Outperform investment rating for Alphabet and increased its price target for the company's stock by $100 to $1,450, while Stifel Nicolaus boosted its price target by $222 to $1,456 a share and kept its Buy rating. Also Tuesday, Canaccord Genuity lifted its price target for Google by $120 to $1,170 a share.
+ Link Motion ( LKM ) still was nearly 1% higher Tuesday afternoon, drifting off a nearly 9% spike soon after the opening bell that followed the Chinese "smart" car company announcing a new strategic partnership with Alibaba's ( BABA ) AutoNavi digital-mapping unit. Under terms of the partnership agreement, AutoNavi will guide riders directly from its popular mapping application to Link Motion's smart ride service in all of Link Motion's current markets. Link Motion also will use AutoNavi's mapping and navigation applications in its "smart" ride business.
